Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: The

outputs.L1:
The present disclosure relates to an imaging apparatus and an information processing system capable of reducing the amount of data, such as video data, transmitted via a network while suppressing power consumption of the imaging apparatus.

An imaging apparatus according to a first aspect of the present disclosure includes: an image sensor having an imaging surface on which a plurality of pixels are arranged vertically and horizontally; a pixel control unit configured to control the image sensor, select, from among pixels constituting each block obtained by partitioning the imaging surface of the image sensor into a plurality of blocks, a pixel corresponding to a sampling function applied to the block, and output a sampling signal based on a pixel value of the selected pixel; and a reduced image generating unit configured to generate a reduced image based on the sampling signal output from the image sensor for each block.
outputs.L2: This disclosure concerns an imaging device and an information processing system designed to reduce the volume of video data or similar content sent over a network while also limiting the power used by the imaging device. In one aspect, the disclosed imaging device includes an image sensor having an imaging surface formed from numerous pixels arranged in vertical and horizontal directions. The device also includes a pixel control unit that operates the image sensor, divides the imaging surface into multiple blocks, applies a sampling function to each block, selects from the pixels in each block a pixel corresponding to that sampling function, and outputs a sampling signal based on the pixel value of the selected pixel. In addition, the device includes a reduced-image generation unit that creates a reduced image using the sampling signal output by the image sensor for each block.
outputs.L3:
The disclosure relates to an imaging apparatus and an information processing system designed to reduce the amount of video data that must be transmitted while also lowering power consumption.

The imaging apparatus includes an image sensor having an imaging surface. This imaging surface is formed from a large number of pixels arranged in both vertical and horizontal directions. These pixels capture image information from a subject or scene.

A pixel control unit is provided to control how pixel information is read from the imaging surface. The pixel control unit partitions the imaging surface into a plurality of blocks. For each block, the pixel control unit applies a sampling function that determines which pixel or pixels in the block are to be used for image data generation.

Based on the sampling function, the pixel control unit selects a pixel corresponding to that function within each block. The unit then outputs a sampling signal based on the pixel value of the selected pixel. In this way, instead of reading and transmitting values from all pixels on the imaging surface, the apparatus uses representative pixel values obtained according to the sampling function.

A reduced image generating unit generates a reduced image by using the sampling signals output from the respective blocks. Because the reduced image is created from selected pixel values rather than the full set of image sensor pixels, the volume of video data to be transmitted can be decreased. This reduction in transmitted data can also reduce processing load and power consumption in the imaging apparatus and the associated information processing system.
outputs.L4:
An imaging apparatus and an associated information processing system are configured to reduce the amount of video data transmitted over a network while also lowering power consumption during image capture and processing. The imaging apparatus includes an image sensor having a pixel array made up of a plurality of pixels. Instead of reading and transmitting image data from every pixel in the array, the pixel array is divided into a plurality of blocks, and pixels within each block are selectively sampled according to a predetermined or dynamically adjustable sampling function.

For each block of the pixel array, the apparatus determines one or more pixels to be read out based on the sampling function. The sampling function may define, for example, a sampling position, a sampling interval, a representative pixel, an average of selected pixels, or another rule for selecting pixel information from within the block. By applying this function block by block, the apparatus generates sampling signals that represent the image information contained in the corresponding blocks without requiring full-resolution readout of the entire pixel array.

The sampling signals are then used to generate a reduced image. This reduced image contains less data than an image produced by reading all pixels of the sensor, but it still preserves sufficient visual information for monitoring, recognition, analysis, or transmission purposes. Because the reduced image has a smaller data volume, it can be transmitted through a network using less bandwidth. This is particularly useful in systems involving network cameras, surveillance devices, mobile imaging devices, edge computing equipment, or other image acquisition devices connected to remote processing apparatuses.

The reduction in readout operations and transmitted data also contributes to lower power consumption. Since fewer pixels are read and processed, the image sensor, signal processing circuitry, memory, and communication interface can operate with reduced workload. This makes the apparatus suitable for battery-powered devices, always-on cameras, distributed sensor networks, and other systems where energy efficiency is important.

The information processing system may receive the reduced image from the imaging apparatus and perform further processing, such as object detection, scene analysis, motion detection, image recognition, storage, or display. In some configurations, the system may control the sampling function based on imaging conditions, network conditions, required image quality, detected motion, region of interest, or processing requirements. For example, the system may increase the sampling density in important regions of the image and reduce the sampling density in less important regions, thereby balancing image quality, bandwidth usage, and power consumption.

Through this block-based pixel sampling approach, the imaging apparatus can efficiently generate image data appropriate for the intended application while avoiding unnecessary acquisition and transmission of full-resolution video. As a result, the apparatus and system provide improved efficiency in imaging operation, reduced network traffic, and decreased power usage without requiring substantial changes to the overall image capture architecture.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, but it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article because it points to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, saying “a book” could mean any book, but saying “the book” means a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

Although “the” is short and simple, it helps make sentences clearer and more precise. It gives context, creates focus, and connects ideas. We use it every day without thinking, in phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” “the answer,” or “the future.” In each case, the word helps identify something specific and meaningful.

In writing, “the” can also add emphasis. A phrase like “the moment” or “the reason” suggests importance and uniqueness. This tiny word shows how even the simplest parts of language can have a big impact on meaning. Without “the,” English would feel less clear, less natural, and less complete.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style summary for an imaging apparatus that reduces video data transmitted over a network by sampling pixels block-by-block on an image sensor and generating a reduced image.
counterfactuals.output:
An imaging apparatus is provided that reduces the amount of video data transmitted over a network while maintaining information useful for monitoring, recognition, or display. The imaging apparatus includes an image sensor having a plurality of pixels arranged in a two-dimensional array, a control circuit configured to define a plurality of pixel blocks within the image sensor, and an image processing circuit configured to generate reduced image data by sampling pixels on a block-by-block basis.

In one embodiment, each pixel block includes a predetermined number of pixels, and at least one representative pixel value is obtained from each pixel block. The representative pixel value may be selected from one or more pixels in the block, calculated as an average or weighted value of pixels in the block, or generated according to a sampling pattern. The sampling pattern may be fixed or dynamically changed based on imaging conditions, motion, object detection results, network bandwidth, or a user setting.

The image processing circuit produces a reduced image having fewer pixels than an original image captured by the image sensor. Because the reduced image is generated at or near the image sensor by selectively reading, sampling, or processing pixels in units of blocks, the volume of image data output from the imaging apparatus is decreased before transmission. A communication interface transmits the reduced image data to an external device over a wired or wireless network.

In certain embodiments, the imaging apparatus further includes a controller configured to set a block size, a sampling ratio, or a sampling location within each block in accordance with a required resolution, frame rate, available communication bandwidth, or power consumption condition. The controller may also switch between transmission of full-resolution image data and reduced image data, or may transmit full-resolution data for selected regions of interest while transmitting reduced data for other regions.

Accordingly, the imaging apparatus can reduce network traffic, processing load, storage requirements, and power consumption while providing video data suitable for surveillance, remote monitoring, machine vision, video conferencing, or other imaging applications.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft the “present disclosure relates to” section for a patent application about a camera system that lowers power consumption and network bandwidth by selecting pixels according to a sampling function for each block of the sensor.
counterfactuals.output:
The present disclosure relates generally to imaging systems and, more particularly, to camera systems and image sensors configured to reduce power consumption, data throughput, and network bandwidth by selectively sampling pixel data. In certain embodiments, the present disclosure relates to a camera system that divides an image sensor into a plurality of blocks and selects, for each block, a subset of pixels according to a corresponding sampling function. The selected pixel data may be read out, processed, encoded, transmitted, or stored while unselected pixel data is omitted, skipped, averaged, estimated, or otherwise not fully communicated, thereby reducing sensor readout activity, processing load, memory usage, and bandwidth requirements.

The present disclosure further relates to methods, apparatuses, and non-transitory computer-readable media for controlling pixel selection in an image capture device. In some implementations, a sampling function associated with a block of the sensor may define which pixels within the block are sampled during an image frame or sequence of frames. The sampling function may be fixed, adaptive, spatially varying, temporally varying, or based on one or more scene characteristics, regions of interest, motion information, illumination conditions, object detection results, compression requirements, available power, network conditions, or image quality constraints.

The present disclosure also relates to image acquisition and communication techniques in which different blocks of a sensor may be sampled using different sampling functions so that pixel density, sampling pattern, or readout frequency varies across an image. Such techniques may enable reduced-power and reduced-bandwidth image capture while preserving sufficient visual information for monitoring, computer vision, video streaming, surveillance, robotics, mobile devices, embedded cameras, Internet-of-Things devices, automotive systems, drones, and other imaging applications.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a first aspect of a disclosed imaging apparatus capable of reducing transmitted video data, where the imaging surface is divided into blocks and sampling signals are output based on selected pixel values.
counterfactuals.output:
A first aspect of the disclosed imaging apparatus is that it reduces the amount of transmitted video data by performing block-based sampling on the imaging surface.

The apparatus includes an imaging device having an imaging surface made up of a plurality of pixels. The imaging surface is divided into a plurality of blocks, each block including multiple pixels. Instead of outputting image signals for all pixels, the apparatus selects one or more pixel values from each block and outputs sampling signals based on those selected pixel values.

By transmitting only the sampling signals corresponding to selected pixels, rather than the full set of pixel data, the apparatus can reduce the volume of video data to be transmitted while still preserving representative image information from the imaging surface.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a Japanese patent translation-style paragraph explaining an imaging apparatus and information processing system that suppresses power consumption by producing reduced images from block-based pixel sampling.
counterfactuals.output: An imaging apparatus and an information processing system are provided which are capable of suppressing power consumption while generating an image suitable for subsequent processing. The imaging apparatus includes an imaging element having a plurality of pixels arranged two-dimensionally, a pixel reading unit configured to divide an imaging region of the imaging element into a plurality of blocks and to read out, from each block, pixel signals of only a predetermined subset of pixels selected in accordance with a sampling pattern, and a reduced-image generating unit configured to generate a reduced image on the basis of the pixel signals read out from the respective blocks. Since the reduced image is produced without reading all pixels of the imaging element, an amount of pixel data transferred from the imaging element and an amount of signal processing performed in a later stage can be reduced, thereby reducing power consumption. The information processing system includes the imaging apparatus and an information processing apparatus configured to acquire the reduced image from the imaging apparatus and to perform at least one of image recognition, object detection, scene determination, and imaging-condition control using the reduced image. Accordingly, the system can execute processing required for monitoring or control while suppressing power consumed by image acquisition, data transmission, and image processing.
